sources.imagery: Sentinel-2 L2A surface reflectance, ESA Copernicus, via Element 84 earth-search on AWS Open Data
sources.fields: USDA NASS Crop Sequence Boundaries, filtered to polygons at least 80% soybean in the 2025 Cropland Data Layer
sources.weather: Thornton, M.M., R. Shrestha, Y. Wei, P.E. Thornton, S-C. Kao and B.E. Wilson. 2022. Daymet: Daily Surface Weather Data on a 1-km Grid for North America, Version 4 R1. ORNL DAAC. https://doi.org/10.3334/ORNLDAAC/2129
sources.soil: USDA NRCS SSURGO via Soil Data Access

notes.fields: Crop Sequence Boundaries are USDA's satellite-derived estimates of single-crop field units. They are not surveyed parcels, FSA records or ownership boundaries. Each polygon is shrunk 20 m inward so roads, ditches and the neighbouring crop stay out of the signal.
notes.ndvi: Cloud-screened per pixel, then the median over each field's interior. A date is usable when at least one field could be measured on it; on most usable dates some fields are still lost to cloud. Values are never interpolated between dates: a gap is cloud, not a change in the crop.
notes.precip: Daymet precipitation sampled on an approximately 1 km grid of latitude/longitude query points and smoothly rendered for visualisation. Daymet is itself a gridded estimate interpolated from weather stations, not a rain gauge in the field, and these sample points are not snapped to its native 1 km projected raster. Cumulative totals run from 1 May, the conventional start of the Iowa soybean planting window -- a stated reference point, not an estimated planting date.
